body:
You are correct that if we apply this to the existing functions it will be breaking.

I'm rather torn on whether it's better to change the existing functions (#116580) or just introduce new safe versions (#116666).

Usually I'm all about introducing new functions and keeping existing to prevent regressions. But I'm not sure which will be best here longterm, as the existing functions are in some senses, buggy (although it is documented as such, to be fair).

Maybe new safe versions would be the best for introduction, and then we could re-evaluate at a later stage whether we wanted to make the existing functions safe. :thinking: 

UPDATE: I've now changed both PRs to simply introducing a new function `safe_normalize` and not breaking compat. On reflection changing the existing implementations to use this or similar probably needs some time using the new version to make the case more convincing, and non-compat breaking is an easier sell.
